raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-MEX-SustainableValueChains",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Low market uptake of the newly introduced Sustainability‑Linked and Green Loans may limit financing reach.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Run targeted outreach and pilot incentives; partner with anchor firms to create demand for sustainable loans.",
      "evidence": "Section 7: first systematic application of SLLs in Mexico; market for sustainable finance remains nascent and concentrated among large corporations."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Participating Financial Institutions lack capacity to design, appraise and monitor green loan portfolios.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide dedicated technical assistance, standardized appraisal tools and training workshops for PFIs.",
      "evidence": "Section 15: limited capacity of Mexican financial institutions to design, originate, appraise and monitor green loans."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "High Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) costs deter SMEs from applying for sustainable finance.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Subsidize MRV expenses, develop a shared verification platform and simplify reporting templates.",
      "evidence": "Section 15: high Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) costs and limited capacity hinder SME loan uptake."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Credit risk of beneficiary enterprises could lead to loan defaults and affect project financial viability.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Apply rigorous credit assessments, require co‑financing, and use step‑down pricing incentives tied to performance.",
      "evidence": "Section 30: NAFIN assumes credit risk of BEs; Section 19 notes extreme temperatures raise loan delinquency rates."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Physical climate hazards (heatwaves, floods) may impair SME operations and repayment capacity.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Integrate climate‑resilience criteria in loan eligibility and offer insurance or contingency funding for high‑risk firms.",
      "evidence": "Section 19: Mexico faces significant climate vulnerability; extreme weather increases operational costs and financial distress for SMEs."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Insufficient co‑financing from firms or PFIs could limit the amount of private capital mobilized.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Enforce minimum co‑financing thresholds, provide matching grant incentives, and engage private investors early in pipeline development.",
      "evidence": "Sections 28‑29: require minimum 20% co‑financing from BEs and 30% from PFIs for sub‑projects."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Gender gap in access to finance may reduce participation of women‑led enterprises, undermining inclusive outcomes.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Set gender‑inclusive eligibility criteria, allocate a quota for women‑led firms, and run gender‑focused outreach campaigns.",
      "evidence": "Section 46: 14% gender gap in finance; women‑owned firms have lower credit access."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Risk of greenwashing if sustainability plans are not properly validated, compromising environmental integrity.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Mandate independent ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification for all sustainability plans; conduct random audits.",
      "evidence": "Section on SLL validation: ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification required to mitigate greenwashing risk."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Procurement capacity gaps at NAFIN may delay contract award and implementation of TA activities.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Appoint a qualified internal procurement professional and provide hands‑on training with World Bank support.",
      "evidence": "Section 57‑58: NAFIN staff lack direct procurement experience; internal procurement professional to be appointed."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Fiduciary risk from reliance on legacy manual financial systems could cause errors or delays in fund tracking.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Upgrade FM systems, automate reconciliations, and conduct periodic internal and external audits.",
      "evidence": "Section 54‑55: residual FM risk moderate; efficiency constraints from legacy manual systems."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Changes to the Sustainable Taxonomy or ESG standards may affect eligibility of projects and loan terms.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Monitor policy developments, keep eligibility criteria flexible, and maintain dialogue with regulators and taxonomy authorities.",
      "evidence": "Section 7: Sustainable Taxonomy provides criteria but policy may evolve, affecting eligibility."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Shift in government priorities could reduce political support or funding for the project.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Secure formal commitments through memoranda of understanding and align project outputs with national development plans.",
      "evidence": "Section 2.A.2: Plan México launched 2025; new administration may shift priorities."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Anchor companies may not demand sustainable suppliers, limiting the incentive for firms to adopt green practices.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Engage anchor firms early, develop supplier‑development programs, and link financing to procurement contracts.",
      "evidence": "Section 9‑10: anchor companies expect sustainable suppliers; many SMEs not prepared."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Complex coordination among NAFIN, PFIs and the World Bank could cause implementation delays.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish clear governance structures, regular coordination meetings, and documented decision‑making protocols.",
      "evidence": "Section 38‑39: Project Implementation Team coordinates NAFIN, PFIs, WB; coordination risks noted."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Substantial environmental and social risk classification may trigger compliance challenges and project delays.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement a robust ESMS, conduct thorough due diligence, and monitor compliance with regular reporting.",
      "evidence": "Section 60: Environmental and Social risk classified as Substantial."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "Currency fluctuations could affect the real cost of MXN‑denominated loans for borrowers and lenders.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Use FX swaps to hedge exposure and limit the share of USD‑denominated loans.",
      "evidence": "Section 31: NAFIN will manage FX risk using Mexico’s currency swap market."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R17",
      "description": "Failure to mobilize the targeted US$89 million of private capital would reduce overall impact.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Develop a pipeline of bankable projects, offer de‑risking instruments, and engage private investors early.",
      "evidence": "Section 28: project aims to mobilize US$89 million private capital; shortfall risk."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R18",
      "description": "Weak anti‑corruption controls could expose the project to fraud or reputational damage.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Strengthen anti‑corruption policies, train staff, and implement a whistle‑blower mechanism with regular audits.",
      "evidence": "Loan Agreement sections require compliance with Anti‑Corruption Guidelines and fraud detection provisions."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Low market uptake of the newly introduced Sustainability‑Linked and Green Loans may limit financing reach.
risks.mitigation: Run targeted outreach and pilot incentives; partner with anchor firms to create demand for sustainable loans.
risks.evidence: Section 7: first systematic application of SLLs in Mexico; market for sustainable finance remains nascent and concentrated among large corporations.

risks.description: Participating Financial Institutions lack capacity to design, appraise and monitor green loan portfolios.
risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated technical assistance, standardized appraisal tools and training workshops for PFIs.
risks.evidence: Section 15: limited capacity of Mexican financial institutions to design, originate, appraise and monitor green loans.

risks.description: High Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) costs deter SMEs from applying for sustainable finance.
risks.mitigation: Subsidize MRV expenses, develop a shared verification platform and simplify reporting templates.
risks.evidence: Section 15: high Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) costs and limited capacity hinder SME loan uptake.

risks.description: Credit risk of beneficiary enterprises could lead to loan defaults and affect project financial viability.
risks.mitigation: Apply rigorous credit assessments, require co‑financing, and use step‑down pricing incentives tied to performance.
risks.evidence: Section 30: NAFIN assumes credit risk of BEs; Section 19 notes extreme temperatures raise loan delinquency rates.

risks.description: Physical climate hazards (heatwaves, floods) may impair SME operations and repayment capacity.
risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑resilience criteria in loan eligibility and offer insurance or contingency funding for high‑risk firms.
risks.evidence: Section 19: Mexico faces significant climate vulnerability; extreme weather increases operational costs and financial distress for SMEs.

risks.description: Insufficient co‑financing from firms or PFIs could limit the amount of private capital mobilized.
risks.mitigation: Enforce minimum co‑financing thresholds, provide matching grant incentives, and engage private investors early in pipeline development.
risks.evidence: Sections 28‑29: require minimum 20% co‑financing from BEs and 30% from PFIs for sub‑projects.

risks.description: Gender gap in access to finance may reduce participation of women‑led enterprises, undermining inclusive outcomes.
risks.mitigation: Set gender‑inclusive eligibility criteria, allocate a quota for women‑led firms, and run gender‑focused outreach campaigns.
risks.evidence: Section 46: 14% gender gap in finance; women‑owned firms have lower credit access.

risks.description: Risk of greenwashing if sustainability plans are not properly validated, compromising environmental integrity.
risks.mitigation: Mandate independent ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification for all sustainability plans; conduct random audits.
risks.evidence: Section on SLL validation: ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification required to mitigate greenwashing risk.

risks.description: Procurement capacity gaps at NAFIN may delay contract award and implementation of TA activities.
risks.mitigation: Appoint a qualified internal procurement professional and provide hands‑on training with World Bank support.
risks.evidence: Section 57‑58: NAFIN staff lack direct procurement experience; internal procurement professional to be appointed.

risks.description: Fiduciary risk from reliance on legacy manual financial systems could cause errors or delays in fund tracking.
risks.mitigation: Upgrade FM systems, automate reconciliations, and conduct periodic internal and external audits.
risks.evidence: Section 54‑55: residual FM risk moderate; efficiency constraints from legacy manual systems.

risks.description: Changes to the Sustainable Taxonomy or ESG standards may affect eligibility of projects and loan terms.
risks.mitigation: Monitor policy developments, keep eligibility criteria flexible, and maintain dialogue with regulators and taxonomy authorities.
risks.evidence: Section 7: Sustainable Taxonomy provides criteria but policy may evolve, affecting eligibility.

risks.description: Shift in government priorities could reduce political support or funding for the project.
risks.mitigation: Secure formal commitments through memoranda of understanding and align project outputs with national development plans.
risks.evidence: Section 2.A.2: Plan México launched 2025; new administration may shift priorities.

risks.description: Anchor companies may not demand sustainable suppliers, limiting the incentive for firms to adopt green practices.
risks.mitigation: Engage anchor firms early, develop supplier‑development programs, and link financing to procurement contracts.
risks.evidence: Section 9‑10: anchor companies expect sustainable suppliers; many SMEs not prepared.

risks.description: Complex coordination among NAFIN, PFIs and the World Bank could cause implementation delays.
risks.mitigation: Establish clear governance structures, regular coordination meetings, and documented decision‑making protocols.
risks.evidence: Section 38‑39: Project Implementation Team coordinates NAFIN, PFIs, WB; coordination risks noted.

risks.description: Substantial environmental and social risk classification may trigger compliance challenges and project delays.
risks.mitigation: Implement a robust ESMS, conduct thorough due diligence, and monitor compliance with regular reporting.
risks.evidence: Section 60: Environmental and Social risk classified as Substantial.

risks.description: Currency fluctuations could affect the real cost of MXN‑denominated loans for borrowers and lenders.
risks.mitigation: Use FX swaps to hedge exposure and limit the share of USD‑denominated loans.
risks.evidence: Section 31: NAFIN will manage FX risk using Mexico’s currency swap market.

risks.description: Failure to mobilize the targeted US$89 million of private capital would reduce overall impact.
risks.mitigation: Develop a pipeline of bankable projects, offer de‑risking instruments, and engage private investors early.
risks.evidence: Section 28: project aims to mobilize US$89 million private capital; shortfall risk.

risks.description: Weak anti‑corruption controls could expose the project to fraud or reputational damage.
risks.mitigation: Strengthen anti‑corruption policies, train staff, and implement a whistle‑blower mechanism with regular audits.
risks.evidence: Loan Agreement sections require compliance with Anti‑Corruption Guidelines and fraud detection provisions.
